item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
364
ABPZ20 KNHC 010501
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Nolo, located several hundred miles west of Lihue, Hawaii, on
Hurricane Rachel, located within a couple of hundred miles southwest
of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico, and on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E,
located well west-southwest of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form late this weekend or early next
week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is likely form while the system moves
slowly west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Public Advisory Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Thu Oct 01 2026 
444 
WTPZ33 KNHC 010839
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM MST Thu Oct 01 2026
 
...RACHEL STRENGTHENING AS IT CONTINUES WEST-NORTHWESTWARD...

SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.4N 109.3W
ABOUT 245 MI...390 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 245 MI...395 KM S OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...972 MB...28.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches of warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the southern portion of Baja California Sur should
monitor the progress of Rachel.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 19.4 North, longitude 109.3 West. Rachel is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h), and this motion is 
expected to continue during the next couple of days. On the forecast 
track, the center of Rachel will continue to move away from mainland 
Mexico and pass south of the Baja California Peninsula today.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Rachel is expected to continue strengthening and become a 
major hurricane within the next couple of days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 972 mb (28.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Gusts to tropical-storm force are possible along portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico today.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel is expected to produce additional rainfall totals
of 2 to 4 inches, with isolated maximum storm totals of 12 inches,
across coastal portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero,
Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect the southwestern coast
of Mexico during the next couple of days and spread northward along
the coast of west-central Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula
through the end of the week. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Thu Oct 01 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 010841
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM MST Thu Oct 01 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Rachel's convective structure has
improved over the past several hours. Deep convection continues to
expand over the center, with cloud-top temperatures as cold as -85
C. The latest subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB is
T4.5/77 kt, while objective estimates have ranged from 65 to 85 kt.
Given these estimates and the improved convective organization, the
initial intensity is raised to 85 kt.

Rachel continues to move west-northwestward, or 300/5 kt, and this 
motion is expected to continue during the next day or so while a 
mid- to upper-level trough remains over the southwestern United 
States. As the trough lifts northeastward and weakens, a ridge is 
forecast to build north of Rachel, causing the system to gradually 
turn more toward the west by the weekend. The track guidance remains 
in good agreement on this overall scenario, and the latest NHC track 
forecast is essentially unchanged from the previous prediction, 
lying near the HCCA and GDMI aids.

Environmental conditions should remain generally favorable for 
strengthening during the next couple of days, with very warm sea 
surface temperatures and plenty of mid-level moisture along the 
forecast track. Persistent easterly to northeast vertical wind shear 
of around 15 kt may be a limiting factor in the short term, but the 
shear is forecast to gradually relax thereafter. Rachel should 
continue to strengthen over the next 24 h, especially if the 
inner-core structure continues to improve, and is forecast to become 
a major hurricane within the next couple of days. Thereafter, 
progressively cooler sea surface temperatures and dry mid-level air 
should induce a gradual weakening trend. The latest NHC intensity 
forecast is similar to the previous advisory, lying above the 
guidance envelope in the short term before trending toward the upper 
end of the guidance thereafter.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

item.title: Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Thu Oct 01 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 010844
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
200 AM PDT Thu Oct 01 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that the convective structure associated 
with Tropical Depression Nineteen-E has changed little during the 
past several hours. Convective organization remains limited, with 
mainly intermittent bursts developing over the center. Additionally, 
scatterometer data showed that the low-level circulation is 
elongated from northeast to southwest, with peak winds up to 25 kt 
south of the circulation. Based on these data, the initial intensity 
is held at 25 kt.

Environmental conditions will continue to limit the cyclone's 
ability to strengthen or become organized over the next day or so 
due to increasing easterly shear and dry mid-level air. The guidance 
supports this scenario, showing the system degenerating into a 
remnant low in 24 h, then dissipating in 36 h as it continues 
eastward toward the vicinity of Hurricane Rachel. The NHC forecast 
is essentially an update of the previous forecast.

The depression is moving eastward at about 12 kt, and that general 
motion is expected to continue in the low-level flow until the 
system dissipates.
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  01/0900Z 15.3N 124.6W   25 KT  30 MPH
 12H  01/1800Z 15.4N 122.9W   25 KT  30 MPH
 24H  02/0600Z 15.2N 120.1W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 36H  02/1800Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
